title: Tuga A8 vs Tuga A10: 8 Inch or 10 Inch Rugged Android Tablet?
description: Tuga A8 (£399) or Tuga A10 (£449)? £50 apart. The A8 has the 700 nit screen, USB-A and a bigger battery; the A10 has 10.1 inches, IP68 and dual SIM.
summary: £50 apart, both Android 14 with 8GB of RAM, a 1920 x 1200 screen and MIL-STD-810H: the A8 has a 700 nit screen against 350, a USB-A port and an 8500mAh battery; the A10 has the 10.1 inch screen, IP68, dual SIM and weighs 680g against 715g.
lede: For sole traders and small firms choosing between the two Android tablets in the range. The short answer: the A8 at £399 for outdoor work, the van and one-handed use, the A10 at £449 for drawings, plans and spreadsheets, wet sites and patchy coverage where dual SIM helps.
verdict: Buy the Tuga A10 at £449 if you read drawings and plans on it; buy the Tuga A8 at £399 if it works outdoors or in the van. The gap is £50, and the two share more than they differ: both run Android 14 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, both have a 1920 x 1200 screen, both are tested to MIL-STD-810H, both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C, and both have a built-in battery, a pogo pin connector, NFC and 4G. The £50 buys a bigger screen (10.1 inches against 8), IP68 against IP67, dual SIM against a single SIM, microSD up to 2TB against 512GB, and a slimmer, lighter body: 14.5mm and 680g against 21.5mm and 715g.

Pay the £50 if you read drawings, plans or spreadsheets on the tablet. Both screens have the same resolution, so the A10 shows the same detail larger rather than more of it, but on a large drawing that still means less zooming. IP68 is rated for immersion beyond IP67, and dual SIM 4G lets you fit two networks for rural sites where one is patchy. Both can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65. The A10's weak point is brightness: at 350 nits it is half the A8's 700, so in direct sun on an open site, a roof or a dashboard mount it is harder to read. It is the tablet for a site cabin or a desk dock. The construction page goes through where it earns its place for drawings.

Keep the £50 if the tablet lives outdoors or in the van. The A8's 700 nit screen is twice as bright as the A10's, its 8500mAh battery is larger than the A10's 8000mAh, and it has a full size USB-A port for a scanner, keyboard or USB stick without an adapter, which the A10 does not list. Its 8 inch size suits one hand up a ladder or a van door pocket, though it is the thicker and slightly heavier of the two. Neither battery is removable, so plan to charge either in a dock or the van. For forms, photos, route maps and quotes, the A8 is the cheaper choice, and the field service page covers where the A8 fits against the A6 and W8. If one job decides it, tell us what you do and we will say which we would buy.
chooseA: You read the screen in direct sun on roofs, open sites or a van dashboard: 700 nits against the A10's 350.
You plug in a USB stick, keyboard or scanner: the A8 has a full size USB-A port as well as USB-C, and the A10 lists no USB-A port.
You want the larger battery: 8500mAh against 8000mAh, both built in.
You hold it in one hand up a ladder or drop it in a van door pocket: 8 inches against 10.1.
Forms, photos and route maps are the job, and £50 is better kept in the business.
chooseB: You read drawings, PDF plans or full spreadsheets on the tablet, and check your own viewer apps run: 10.1 inches against 8, at the same 1920 x 1200 resolution.
It gets dropped in water or left out in it: IP68 against the A8's IP67. Both are tested to MIL-STD-810H.
You work where one network is patchy: dual SIM 4G, where the A8 takes a single SIM.
You carry it all day: 680g and 14.5mm thick against 715g and 21.5mm, with a hand strap in the box.
You store a lot of photos, plans or offline maps on the device: microSD up to 2TB against 512GB on the A8.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A10 worth £50 more than the Tuga A8?
faq.a: For drawings and plans, or if you want IP68 and dual SIM, yes; for forms, photos and route maps in the open, the A8 does the job for £50 less. The A10 costs £449 and the A8 £399. Both run Android 14 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage on a 1920 x 1200 screen, and both are tested to MIL-STD-810H. The £50 buys a 10.1 inch screen in place of 8 inches, IP68 against IP67, dual SIM against a single SIM, microSD up to 2TB against 512GB, and a lighter, slimmer body. It gives up brightness (350 nits against 700), the A8's USB-A port and 500mAh of battery. If you spend the day in PDF plans, BIM viewers or spreadsheets, pay it and buy the Tuga A10. If you work outdoors, fill in forms, take photos and follow routes, buy the Tuga A8 and keep the £50. Buying several? Device discounts run from 3 percent at two to 10 percent at ten or more, see bulk orders.

faq.q: Can I read the Tuga A10 screen outdoors?
faq.a: It is 350 nits, half the A8's 700, so direct sun is harder work than on the A8. Indoors or in a site cabin it is the better screen for plans: the same 1920 x 1200 resolution on 10.1 inches against 8, so a drawing shows larger. If most of your day is on open sites or roofs, choose the A8, or keep the A10 for the cabin and the desk dock. The construction page says the same thing with the trades spelled out.

faq.q: Which lasts longer on a charge, the A8 or the A10?
faq.a: We cannot say. The A8 has 8500mAh and the A10 8000mAh, but neither lists a run time in hours and the two have different screens and processors, so we will not guess. Neither battery is removable, so plan to charge in place. The A10 lists quick charge with a 9V/2.2A adapter; the A8 lists 5V/3A charging over USB-C or its DC jack, plus pogo pin dock charging. Both take the 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the Charging Dock (£49.99) and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), which has a DC power input, all on the accessories page. Both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. Our guide to rugged tablets in winter covers what the cold does to any battery.

faq.q: Are the A8 and A10 the same size and weight?
faq.a: No. The A10 is the bigger but lighter tablet: 250 x 167mm, 14.5mm thick and 680g. The A8 is 225.6 x 144.6mm, 21.5mm thick and 715g, so it is smaller in the hand but thicker and 35g heavier. With an 8 inch screen against 10.1 it is still the one for one hand and a van door pocket. The same Vehicle Mounting Dock, Charging Dock, Hand Strap and Rugged Carry Case (fits tablets up to 10.1 inches) are listed for both; a hand strap comes in the A10's box, and for the A8 the Hand Strap (£24) is sold separately.
